svg.title: flightrec walkthrough
svg.desc: What flightrec solves and how: per-request debug log buffering, triggers, cross-service flush, crash recovery and OpenTelemetry spans.

g.text: Debug logs for the requests that fail.
One line for the ones that don't.
Every team picks one of two bad options
the context is gone, and the bug
You need debug logs for the 1% of requests that fail; you don't know which ones in advance.
Debug logs are kept per request and written only when the request fails
flightrec Recorder: one buffer per request
in memory, bounded per request and per process
in order, with the trace ID and reason
Existing log calls stay as they are
Wrap your handler, set it as the default logger, wrap your router.
A failure deep in the call chain keeps the logs of every service that handled the request
async calls and callers that already finished:
Options.Retain keeps their buffers; the notice flushes them
Retained buffers flush with reason remote:<reason>; every notice is rate limited and validated
kill -9, out-of-memory kills and expired grace periods no longer lose in-flight requests
every buffered record is also copied
Torn writes skipped by checksum · a crash during recovery is retried 3 times · stop() zeros the file
otelflightrec.SpanProcessor sits in front of your exporter
linked to the same trace as the logs
Measured with BatchSpanProcessor + OTLP/HTTP on a GitHub runner: healthy trace 34.9 µs CPU vs 79.5 µs
Measured on GitHub runners and in a three-service end-to-end test (docs/e2e-report.md)
Apache-2.0 · Go 1.26+ · journal on Linux, macOS and the BSDs
